The nitrated metabolite of gT, NO2-g-CEHC, can be generated from gT after nitration to 5-NO2-gT and subsequent metabolism.
However, since 5-NO2-gT is apparently inefﬁciently incorporated into liver cells, it is not detected in urine while g-CEHC is abun-
dant and it is to date unknown whether it exerts any cellular activity at higher concentrations. In smokers, aT supplementation
reduces circulating gT in part by increasing its metabolism and competition with uptake with consequent lower 5-NO2-gT forma-
tion by scavenging of RNS.
As recently critically reviewed, some of the metabolites act as bioactive molecules that modulate the activity of transcrip-
tion factors, membrane channels and enzymes even at the low nanomolar concentrations reached in plasma and in the intes-
tine (low micromolar concentrations can be reached after supplementation) (Birringer and Lorkowski, 2019). Among the
activities of metabolites (LCM, CEHC) are: natriuretic activity of g-CEHC, anti-inﬂammatory and antioxidative activities by
